patterns.label: São Paulo (11), Rio de Janeiro (21), Brasília (61)

examples.note: São Paulo — DDD area code 11
São Paulo mobile — the leading 9 was added on 2012-07-29, making mobile NSNs 11 digits
Toll-free — always billed as a local call regardless of where the call centre sits

notes: Brazil requires a carrier selection code (CSP) for long-distance calls: you dial 0, then a 2-digit carrier code (21 Claro, 41 TIM, 15 Vivo), then the area code and number.
Area codes are called DDD codes and are always 2 digits.
Mobile numbers gained a leading 9 in 2012, so mobile NSNs are 11 digits against 10 for landlines — this is the reliable way to tell them apart.
sources: ANATEL — Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações: https://www.gov.br/anatel/

formats.international: +54 AA XXXX XXXX — mobiles take an extra 9: +54 9 AA XXXX XXXX

examples.note: Buenos Aires — 2-digit area code 11 with an 8-digit subscriber number
Mar del Plata mobile — note the 9 replaces the domestic 15 when dialling from abroad
Toll-free

notes: Argentine mobile numbers are written two different ways: domestically the digit 15 sits between the area code and the subscriber number, but from abroad you drop the 15 and insert a 9 immediately after +54.
So (0223) 15 123-4567 dialled locally becomes +54 9 223 123 4567 internationally — the same line, two forms. This trips up a lot of validation code.
The national number is always 10 digits (excluding the mobile 9); area codes run 2–4 digits with the subscriber number sized to match.
sources: ENACOM — Ente Nacional de Comunicaciones: https://www.enacom.gob.ar/

formats.national: X XXXX XXXX (9 digits, no area codes)

patterns.label: Fixed line (2 = Santiago, other digits by region)

examples.note: Santiago — fixed lines renumbered onto the 2 prefix in 2012–2013
Mobile — the 9 prefix, though portability blurs the fixed/mobile distinction
Toll-free

notes: Chile has no geographic area codes and no trunk prefix — every call within Chile is a local call and all numbers are a flat 9 digits.
Full number portability across fixed, mobile and VoIP means the leading digit no longer reliably identifies the line type.
The international access prefix is carrier-selected in the form 1XX0.

examples.note: Bogotá — the 601 prefix covers Bogotá and Cundinamarca
Medellín and Antioquia — prefix 604
Mobile — 3XX ranges; 310 is a Claro range

notes: Colombia renumbered in September 2021–2022: the old single-digit dialling zones with 7-digit local numbers became uniform 10-digit numbers by inserting '60' in front of the zone digit.
So the old Bogotá (1) 234 5678 is now 601 234 5678.
Mobile numbers were already 10 digits and were unaffected by the reform.
sources: MinTIC — Ministerio de Tecnologías de la Información y las Comunicaciones: https://www.mintic.gov.co/

patterns.label: Regional (2-digit area codes, e.g. Cusco 84, Arequipa 54)

examples.note: Lima — area code 1, the only area with 7-digit subscriber numbers
Cusco — area code 84 with a 6-digit subscriber number
Mobile — all Peruvian mobiles are 9 digits beginning with 9

notes: Lima/Callao has a single-digit area code and 7-digit subscriber numbers; every other region has a 2-digit code and 6-digit numbers.
Mobile numbers became fully non-geographic under the 2010 'Área Virtual Móvil' reform and are dialled as a flat 9 digits nationwide.
sources: OSIPTEL — Organismo Supervisor de Inversión Privada en Telecomunicaciones: https://www.osiptel.gob.pe/

examples.note: Caracas — area code 212
Mobile — 412 is a Digitel range
Mobile — 414/424 are Movistar ranges

notes: Closed 10-digit plan: a 3-digit area code plus a 7-digit subscriber number. The plan was last revised on 2000-09-21.
Mobile operator codes fall in the 412–426 range.
Numbers beginning with 5 are region-free and billed as local calls nationwide.
sources: CONATEL — Comisión Nacional de Telecomunicaciones: https://www.conatel.gob.ve/

patterns.label: South-East — VIC, TAS (03); North-East — QLD (07); Central-West — WA, SA, NT (08)

examples.note: Sydney — area code 02 covers NSW and the ACT
Melbourne — area code 03 covers Victoria and Tasmania
Mobile — all Australian mobiles begin 04 and are nationwide
Freecall

notes: Australia has just four geographic area codes (02, 03, 07, 08), each covering a large multi-state region.
The international access prefix is 0011, not 00.
13/1300 numbers are charged at a fixed local rate rather than being free.
sources: ACMA — Australian Communications and Media Authority: https://www.acma.gov.au/numbering

patterns.label: Wellington (04), Waikato/BoP (07), Taranaki–Hawke's Bay (06), South Island (03)

examples.note: Auckland — area code 09 covers Auckland and Northland
Wellington — area code 04
Mobile — 021 is a One NZ range; 022 and 027 are also mobile
Toll-free

notes: New Zealand has five geographic area codes (03, 04, 06, 07, 09) covering large regions; landline NSNs are 8 digits.
Mobile subscriber numbers vary in length, giving mobile NSNs of 9 (sometimes 8 or 10) digits.
sources: Telecommunications Carriers' Forum — NZ numbering: https://www.tcf.org.nz/
